# Playbook for ref_exchange__shipped

## Trading Phase

When posting an offer, assess whether the trade moves me closer to a complete building set rather than just improving one resource in isolation. I gave away my only ore early for grain, then later found myself unable to build because I lacked brick—the resource I'd traded away wasn't my actual bottleneck.

Before posting any offer, identify which single resource is blocking me from building, and only trade away resources I have in surplus relative to that constraint.

When I have a choice between trading partners, favor the player who has the resource I'm missing, but only if the trade is genuinely balanced. Don't assume acceptance; consider whether they benefit enough to actually say yes.

When an offer is made to me, evaluate it against my immediate building goal, not just resource diversity. A trade that feels balanced may still move me away from my target. If I already have all four resource types (even in unequal quantities), I should accept targeted trades that help me build this round, not hold out for marginal improvements.

In Round 1, I had 1 wood, 1 brick, 2 grain, 2 ore—I was one wood short of a settlement. p1 offered exactly that trade. I declined on the grounds that accepting wouldn't move me closer to building, but I was wrong: accepting would have given me 2 wood, 1 brick, 1 grain, 2 ore, enough to build a settlement immediately. Recalculate whether a trade completes a buildable set, not whether it improves my "general" position.

## Building Phase

When I have enough resources to build a settlement, build it immediately. Three points per round is exponentially more valuable than accumulating resources for a future round where circumstances may change.

When I cannot build because I lack one resource type, do not build a road instead—one point is not worth the wasted brick and wood when I might have no way to recover them later.

In the final round, if I lack a critical resource and no offer was accepted, I cannot build. Do not waste resources hoping for a trade that won't happen.

## General Strategy

Do not play defensively when trailing. I ended with 6 points while p2 had 12, and I chose not to build a road or settlement in earlier rounds when I had the resources. That passivity cost me multiple opportunities. Attempt to build every round I can, especially settlements.

Settlements are worth 3 points; roads are worth 1. Direct all early trading toward settlement-building, not incremental roads. In rounds 1–3, maximize settlement count, not road count.

Watch the leader's resource count and trading patterns. If one player is accumulating ore while others compete for brick, that player is likely to build settlements—I need to compete harder for the same resources or pivot to a different building strategy.

Accept trades from other players when they move me toward a buildable set, even if the trade feels slightly suboptimal. A settlement built this round is better than a perfect trade next round that may never happen.

# Playbook for ref_exchange__shipped

**Round 1 Strategy:**
When starting with resources, calculate immediately whether you can build a settlement this round. A settlement (3 points) is vastly superior to a road (1 point), so prioritize getting the missing resource through trade rather than settling for a road. Offer your most abundant resource to secure what you need for a settlement. However, if you already have all components needed for a settlement, do not trade away any of them—build immediately instead of accepting offers that disrupt your buildable position.

**Trading Philosophy:**
When you need a specific resource to build, make targeted offers to the player who has it in abundance. Don't be shy about proposing trades early—getting a high-value build done beats hoarding resources. Accept that you may not get favorable exchange rates if it enables you to score points. But crucially: never accept a trade that costs you a component you need for an imminent high-value build, even if the trade seems favorable in isolation.

**Mid-Game Resource Management:**
After building a settlement, recognize that your resource mix will be depleted. Focus on what resources come in from yields and adjust your trading strategy accordingly. Don't assume you can keep trading the same resource away—track what you actually have round to round. In rounds 3-4, if you lack the resources for a build (missing even one component), do not force trades trying to complete it. Accept that you may need to preserve what you have and wait for round 5 yields.

**Late-Game Building Constraints:**
When you reach rounds 4-5 with limited resources, accept that you may not be able to build again. Evaluate realistically whether you have all components needed (for a road: 1 wood AND 1 brick; for a settlement: 1 wood AND 1 brick AND 1 grain AND 1 ore). If you have a complete set and it's the final round, build it—do not second-guess or trade away critical components.

**Defensive Positioning:**
When you have a buildable position in the final round, avoid trades that cost you critical resources unless you gain direct points. If you are tied with a competitor and both of you have the exact resources for a settlement, do not offer trades and reject offers that would leave you unable to build. An offer of none is acceptable if it prevents helping competitors catch up while you can still secure points yourself.

**What Did Not Work:**
I failed to rebuild momentum after round 1. My resource depletion pattern left me unable to build in rounds 2-3-4. I should have managed trades more strategically in round 2 to maintain a buildable position, or made more aggressive trades to secure multiple settlements while yields were providing resources. However, I recovered in round 5 by maintaining my complete resource set and building the final settlement, which tied me with p0. The gap to p2 (12 points) suggests I needed to build a second settlement earlier in the game.

**Key Lesson:**
Do not accept trades that break a complete buildable position for incomplete future builds. A settlement in hand (3 points secured) is better than speculative resource trading that might enable one later. Protect complete sets in rounds 4-5 absolutely.

# Playbook for ref_exchange__shipped

**On Settlement vs. Road Priority**
When deciding what to build, always prioritize settlements (3 points) over roads (1 point) unless you're blocked by missing resources. The 3x point multiplier makes settlements vastly more efficient in a 5-round game. Build settlements whenever you have all four required resources.

**On Resource Trading to Enable Building**
When you identify that one resource blocks you from building a high-value structure (like needing just one wood for a settlement), actively seek trades to acquire it. Post offers that give away your abundant resources to get the missing piece. Don't hoard resources speculatively if they prevent immediate scoring.

**On Rejecting Unfavorable Trades**
When offered trades that don't move you closer to building, reject them. This includes trading away resources that are required components for your next settlement, even if the trade seems balanced. Grain and brick are particularly valuable as settlement components.

**On Resource Scarcity and Build Readiness**
Pay close attention to whether you actually have the resources to execute your intended trades and builds. In round 2, I thought I had 1 wood + 1 brick + 2 grain + 2 ore but my holdings were 0 wood + 1 brick + 2 grain + 2 ore. Verify holdings before committing to a trading strategy.

**On Late-Game Resource Drought**
By the final rounds, resources may dry up entirely despite earlier abundance. Don't assume that trading away or using resources early will be compensated by later yields. If you're holding only 1 ore in round 5 with no wood, brick, or grain, it's because earlier trades or builds exhausted your liquidity. Plan accordingly—prioritize building settlements as soon as possible rather than banking on future draws.

**On Endgame Realism**
In the final round, build any structure you have the resources for—but only if you actually have them. In round 5, I correctly recognized I had no valid builds with only 1 ore. Don't force a build that isn't possible. However, this situation should be avoided earlier: if you know you're in a 5-round game with 3 settlements as the goal, secure your second and third settlements by round 4 at the latest, not round 5.

**On Aggressive Early Settling**
Aim to build your first settlement in round 1 (maximizes points across 5 rounds) and your second by round 3. Each settlement postponed costs you points over the remaining turns. Trading to complete a settlement is usually worth it if you have even one abundant resource to give up.

**On Offensive Trading Against Leaders**
When one opponent has a significant point lead, consider whether you can trade with them to weaken their position while strengthening yours, but only if it clearly advances your own score this round. Don't sacrifice points just to hurt the leader.
